subject.title: refactor: move non-session runtime journals to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw accept the agent schema v12 cutover and the ACP and memory public-contract changes in this PR, or require compatibility-preserving APIs and complete writer and reader migration first?
rationale: Repository policy requires explicit owner acceptance for SQLite schema-version advances, while the current branch also changes persisted state and existing inspection contracts.

options.title: Preserve contracts before merge
options.body: Keep or replace the ACP and memory inspection handles with supported SQLite-backed APIs, finish every writer and reader migration, and prove upgrade behavior before landing.

options.title: Approve the breaking cutover
options.body: Explicitly accept the removed handles and operator changes, document the upgrade boundary, and require real migration and rollback proof.

options.title: Split the migration
options.body: Pause this broad branch and land smaller owner-reviewed PRs for audit, memory, and ACP storage independently.

recommendation.title: Preserve contracts before merge
recommendation.body: Keep or replace the ACP and memory inspection handles with supported SQLite-backed APIs, finish every writer and reader migration, and prove upgrade behavior before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged session/transcript SQLite flip provides the closest ownership and migration precedent for this decision.
